# local_source_registry

This is a complete file-level inventory of the enumerated literature tree plus explicit parent/component/collection records and inspected project infrastructure. It is not a runtime qualification. The only omitted tree entries are .DS_Store OS metadata; generated .pyc files are retained as unqualified other artifacts. Archives remain unexpanded.

## Reading the registry

One row is one source record. Papers, repos, notebooks, utilities, datasets and checkpoints remain distinct. Source IDs beginning F- identify individual literature file entries; P- identifies project evidence. R- is a repository snapshot, C- a named component, D- a collection, and S-LITERATURE the pool. IDs are deterministic path-derived identifiers, **not content hashes**.

The full record is the row plus its explicitly named metadata profile below. All requested fields—including license state for code/weights/data/bundled components, role, use, dependencies, extraction, validation, priority, qualification, blockers and exact next gate—are defined by that profile. baseline_manifest.json expands every record without inheritance. Row evidence never inherits semantic verification from its parent.

Availability: readable means a full byte read succeeded, not that a model/artifact is valid. Partially readable includes metadata-only records whose bytes were not inspected; reason is always shown. Unavailable means an attempted bounded read failed. Missing assets is used only for specifically documented absent local dependencies.

Observed facts are paths, byte hashes, source declarations and static evidence. Pipeline placement, extraction suitability and proposed use are inferences. Unknown values are explicit and not success. Commit/tag unknown for every repo with no local Git evidence; dependency pin or linked GitHub image commit is never used as the repository commit.
